title: The Dawn Bell
description: Every sunrise for sixty years, the Dawn Bell rings and the town crier reads the morning news. Tonight Mildred calls in to celebrate the tradition, the town clerk mentions the crier died in 2019, and a listener points out the bell has started reading tomorrow's news. And getting it right.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: You're on Snazzie FM, and tonight we honor a real treasure. Sixty years, every single sunrise, the Dawn Bell rings and our town crier reads the morning news off the square. Mildred, you keep that bell. Welcome.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Sixty years. Same bell, same fella, every morning. That's dedication.

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: Oh, it's an honor, Ronnie. Old Edsel's been ringing that bell since before I was born. <p:0.3> Bless the bell. He has never once missed a dawn.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Never missed a dawn. You hear that, Barry? <p:0.3> That's the kind of man you build a town around.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: That's lovely. <p:0.3> How old is Edsel now, exactly? Just rough.

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: Oh, you don't ask a crier his age, dear. <p:0.3> He's up on the square at five every morning, rain or shine. Reads the news, rings her three times, and off he goes. Same as always.

lines.speaker: caller-edwin
lines.text: Hi, yes, hello, this is Edwin, I'm the town clerk. <p:0.3> I keep the bell schedule, per the bylaws. <p:0.3> And I just want to gently flag, for the record, that Edsel passed. In 2019.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: [surprise-ah] I'm sorry. He WHAT?

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: Well, he passed, yes, dear, but he didn't stop. <p:0.3> Bless the bell. You don't let a little thing like that break a sixty-year streak.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Now THAT'S commitment, Barry. The man works through anything.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Ronnie, that is not commitment. That is the opposite of commitment. That is being dead.

lines.speaker: caller-edwin
lines.text: So, per the bylaws, the position should have gone vacant. <p:0.3> But the bell kept ringing at five. On its own. We have the recordings. The square is empty in every single one.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: An empty square and a ringing bell. <p:0.3> See, some traditions just take care of themselves. That's beautiful.

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: It does the reading too, Ronnie. Right on schedule. <p:0.3> I bring it a coffee. It's polite to bring the bell a coffee.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Who reads the news, Mildred? <p:0.3> If Edsel's gone and the square's empty, who is reading the morning news?

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: The bell reads it, dear. In his voice. <p:0.3> It's a comfort, honestly. Sounds just like him.

lines.speaker: caller-edwin
lines.text: And here's the part I flagged twice in the minutes. <p:0.3> The news it reads at five in the morning... hasn't happened yet. <p:0.3> It reads the day BEFORE the day.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: [question-ah] Hold on. Hold on. It reads tomorrow's news?

lines.speaker: caller-edwin
lines.text: Correct. And, per the record, it is never wrong. <p:0.3> Last Tuesday it read that the Henderson barn burned down. The barn was fine. <p:0.3> It burned down Wednesday.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Ahead of the news. <p:0.3> Barry, our crier scooped the entire county. From beyond. That's journalism.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: That is not journalism, Ronnie! A bell predicted a fire and then the fire HAPPENED!

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: It doesn't predict, dear. <p:0.3> It announces. <p:0.3> And then the town... sort of catches up.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: The town CATCHES UP? Mildred, what does that mean, the town catches up?!

lines.speaker: caller-edwin
lines.text: It means whatever the bell reads, happens. <p:0.3> We stopped calling it the news, per the committee. <p:0.3> We call it the schedule now.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: A town that runs right on time. <p:0.3> You can't buy that kind of civic spirit, Barry.

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: And it rang special tonight, Ronnie. <p:0.3> Off schedule. First time in sixty years it ever rang at night. Bless the bell.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Why would it ring at night? <p:0.3> Edwin. Why would a bell that only rings at dawn ring at NIGHT?

lines.speaker: caller-edwin
lines.text: I checked the schedule it read. <p:0.3> Tomorrow's front page is a radio station. <p:0.3> It names a host, a co-host, and a clerk.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: [surprise-ah] Names them doing WHAT, Edwin?

lines.speaker: caller-edwin
lines.text: It just says... joining the crier. <p:0.3> All three. At dawn.

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: Oh, that's an honor, dear!

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: [dissatisfaction-hnn] That is NOT an honor, Mildred!

lines.speaker: caller-edwin
lines.text: It's the schedule!

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Unplug it!

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: You can't unplug a bell, dear!

lines.speaker: caller-edwin
lines.text: It's bronze!

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Ronnie, it's reading US! The bell put us on the SCHEDULE!

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: Bring it a coffee!

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Easy, easy. <p:0.3> Barry, in sixty years that bell has never once been wrong. <p:0.3> So let's not embarrass ourselves by being late.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Late to WHAT, Ronnie?

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: To dawn, Barry. <p:0.5> We'll be right back. <p:0.3> Apparently.

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: ...He never misses a dawn.
